comments.author: tw25497050
comments.story_title: I rewrote a Clojure tool in Rust
comments.why_zh: 关于代码结构的力量和重要性
comments.text_zh: 有时候架构/算法本身很重要，有时候架构/算法需要与语言相匹配。在没有看到更完整的代码库[1]的情况下，我倾向于认为作者更大的设计导致了这些昂贵的函数以它们现有的方式存在[2]。这纯粹是我的猜测，但如果一个人有大量使用命令式、可变语言的经验，那他设计出来的系统在用函数式、不可变语言编写时，可能就不会那么好。如果是这样，那么直接移植到命令式、可变语言时看到改进，也就不那么令人惊讶了。岔开一句：关于代码结构的力量和重要性，我强烈推荐观看 Rafal Dittwald 在 Clojure North 2019 上的 "Solving Problems the Clojure Way"[3]。[1] 我没看到链接，但如果有的话，我很想看看。[2] 比如 `rule-field-diff` 这个函数似乎被一些奇怪的选择拖累了，例如它接收两个 "rules" 作为参数（看起来是以字段为键的规则集合），然后使用两个硬编码的 "operations"（同样以字段为键），并产生一个值为按字段分组的序列的 map（我猜是这样）。我一时想不出这个函数为什么一开始就要跨多个字段工作（也就是说，任何字段特定的"循环"都应该放在外围的上下文中）。`diff-rules-by-keys` 也是如此。[3] [VIDEO]
comments.text: Sometimes the architecture/algorithm matters, and sometimes the architecture/algorithm needs to align with the language. Absent seeing the broader code base [1], I'm inclined to think that the author's larger design led to these expensive functions existing as they did [2]. Pure speculation on my part, but if one has a lot of experience with imperative, mutable languages, one might design a system that ends up being not so great when written in a functional, immutable language. If so, then seeing improvements when directly porting to an imperative, mutable language might be not so surprising. Tangent: Regarding the power and importance of code structure, I highly recommend watching "Solving Problems the Clojure Way" by Rafal Dittwald at Clojure North 2019 [3]. [1] I didn't see a link, but if it's available, I'd love to take a look. [2] The `rule-field-diff` function for example seems to be burdened with some odd choices, e.g., taking in two "rules" as arguments, (which seem to be collections of rules keyed by field), then using two hard-coded "operations" (also keyed by field), and yielding a map whose values are sequences by field (I think). Off the top of my head I don't see why this fn needs to work across multiple fields in the first place (i.e., any field-specific "loop" should be in a surrounding context. Ditto for `diff-rules-by-keys`. [3] [VIDEO]

comments.author: blunte
comments.story_title: Case against OOP is understated, not overstated (2020)
comments.why_zh: 在 JavaScript 中用同一个问题比较过程式、OOP 和 FP 的解法。
comments.quote_zh: 我也敦促你看看这个精彩的视频，它用一个示例问题展示了过程式、OOP（轻量版）和 FP 三种解法
comments.text_zh: --（即使你不读完整条评论，我也敦促你看看这个精彩的视频，它用一个示例问题展示了过程式、OOP（轻量版）和 FP 三种解法：[VIDEO]（尽管名字如此，它演示的是 JavaScript，不是 Clojure）。如果你采用这种方式，你甚至不必告诉别人你在做 FP。你最终会得到更好、更易理解、更易测试的代码。）-- OOP 早期（早期指的是 C++ 时代）的好处，大概在于它让程序员在编码前停下来做规划。我在学完 OOP 20 年后才学 FP，我确信在 FP 里我可以用更少、更易理解（而且容易测试得多）的代码做同样的事。OOP 在一小部分场景和学术场景中很棒。但就像 REST 一样，它不能很好地映射到所有需求。于是它就变得别扭又没必要地复杂。而 FP，或者简化为不变的数据变换、把必要的变更推到边缘，随时随地都能用。在 FP 里你仍然可以选择用层级来建模你的数据，保留 OOP 的一些有用之处。但它依然是数据进、结果出。除非你在两边都做过真实项目，否则你无法体会 FP 为何更优。（而且说清楚，我甚至不是在说 Haskell 那种痴迷类型的 FP。也许因为我不是 Haskell 人，我欣赏不来。但它给我的感觉像是好东西走向极端（因此通常不是当下情境下的最佳选择）；不过我扯远了。）具体来说
comments.text: -- (Even if you don't read this whole comment, I urge you to watch this fantastic video which illustrates procedural, OOP(lite), and FP approaches to a sample problem: [VIDEO] (Despite the name, it illustrates JavaScript, not Clojure). If you follow this approach, you don't even have to tell people you are doing FP. You'll just end up with better, more understandable, and more easily testable code.) -- The early (early as in C++ days) benefit of OOP was probably that it made programmers stop and plan before coding. Having learned FP 20 years after learning OOP, I feel certain that I can do the same things in less and more understandable (and MUCH more easily testable) code in FP. OOP was awesome for a small set of cases and for academic scenarios. But like REST, it doesn't map well to all needs. Then it becomes awkward and unnecessarily complicated. FP, or simplified as immutable data transformations with necessary mutations pushed to the edges, works everywhere, all the time. In FP you can still choose to model your data in hierarchies, keeping some of the useful bits of OOP. But it's still data in, results out. Until you've spent time on real projects in both, you cannot appreciate why FP is superior. (And to be clear, I'm not even talking about Haskell and type-obsessed FP. Perhaps because I'm not a Haskell guy, I can't appreciate it. But it smells to me like an extreme of a good thing (and therefore not usually the best thing for the situation); but I digress.) comments.author: michaelteter
comments.why_zh: 用一个有分量的玩具示例演示了 JavaScript 中从命令式到函数式的重构。
comments.quote_zh: 有一个我很喜欢的视频很好地演示了这种 functional core/imperative shell 的做法
comments.text_zh: 只要条件允许，我就喜欢用这种方式来构建。遗憾的是，我发现很多人——尤其是 tech lead——都抵触这种做法。第一个也是最常见的原因是：“我为什么需要这个？我们现在这样做挺好的。”或者当态度比较积极时，常见的问题是：“我觉得我们的开发者很难接受这个。”这两种情形都让我觉得失望又沮丧，因为技术（以及软件）通常就是为了改进流程和系统，从而更容易地得到更好的结果。但到了这个地步，感觉像是徒劳无功，或者说是一场不值得拼死去争的山头。对我自己的项目，我会走这条路；对别人的项目，我就用更笨的办法干活，让公司的苹果车稳稳立着别翻。吐槽归吐槽，有一个我很喜欢的视频很好地演示了这种 functional core/imperative shell 的做法：Solving Problems the Clojure Way - Rafal Dittwald。那是个 Clojure 的演讲，但演讲中间有一段把命令式代码重构成函数式的 JavaScript 现场演示。虽然只是个玩具例子，但规模足够大，结果能体现出做法上的实质差异。[VIDEO]
comments.text: I like to build this way when possible. Unfortunately, I find many people - especially tech leads - resistant to this approach. The first and most common reason is, "Why do I need this? What we are doing is fine." Or when the attitude is positive about it, the common issue is, "I think this would be too difficult for our devs to adopt." I find both of these scenarios disappointing and frustrating, because technology (and software) is usually about improving processes and systems so better results can be made more easily. But at this point it feels like a lost cause, or rather a hill not worth dying on. For my own projects, I go this path; for others, I work dumber and keep the corporate apple cart upright. Rant aside, there is a video which I really like that demonstrates this functional core/imperative shell approach: Solving Problems the Clojure Way - Rafal Dittwald. It is a Clojure talk, but it gives an imperative to functional refactor demo in JavaScript in the middle of the talk. Even though it is a toy example, it is big enough that the result shows a meaningful difference in approach. [VIDEO]

comments.author: teodorlu
comments.why_zh: 说明寻找领域操作和实体可以指导抽象。
comments.quote_zh: Rafael Dittwald 在这里很好地描述了寻找领域操作和领域实体的过程
comments.text_zh: > 我很希望有一种语言，把这种渐进式演化抽象作为核心关注点。那样就很容易了。你可以从最简单的命令式代码开始，并在需要出现时轻松地把它抽象出来。这就是我写 Clojure 的方式。我先写一些能完成我想要的事情的代码。要么是“完成这件事”的带副作用的代码，要么是从数据到数据的函数。过一阵子，我会觉得自己缺了一两个领域操作。到那时，我就知道自己在缺什么样的抽象。Rafael Dittwald 在这里很好地描述了寻找领域操作和领域实体的过程：[VIDEO]
comments.text: > I would love a language that has this gradual evolutional abstracting as a core concern. That makes it easy. Where you can start from simplest imperative code and easily abstract it as the need for this arises. This is about how I write Clojure. I start out with some code that does the thing I want. Either effectfull code that "does the thing" or functions from data to data. After a while, I feel like I'm missing a domain operation or two. At that point I've got an idea about what kind of abstraction I'm missing. Rafael Dittwald describes the process of looking for domain operations and domain entities nicely here: [VIDEO]

comments.author: ptttr

comments.why_zh: 关于用 Clojure 方式解决问题的 Clojure 演讲。
comments.text_zh: 我理解你的担忧，但我对此的看法恰恰相反。我想我们可以同意，作为一个有经验的开发者，找到"任何"工作都不太难。然而，找到一份很棒、令人满意的工作就难得多。为此你需要绕开很多"公司废话"式的项目，而 Clojure 在这方面很好地充当了一个有用的筛子。我的推理是，Clojure 足够小众，以至于当一家公司在用它时，你可以假设这是出于刻意的技术选择，而不只是因为它流行。这告诉了我两件事，在我看来，这两件事是健康的技术公司文化的症状：- 技术决策由工程师做出，而不是由高层管理者做出；- 他们的结论和赌注与我的相合，因为我们都看到并认同 Clojure 相对于更流行的方案的优势。诚然，总存在有人只是跟风、然后力不从心的风险，但我认为这个风险相对较小，因为 Clojure 已经不是新面孔了，而且选择技术栈是一个重大决定，通常由资深技术领导层来做，希望没那么受炒作驱动。当然，Clojure 不是什么银弹，它只是一个给你足够绳子让你上吊的工具。混乱的代码库和其他语言一样可能出现，尤其是当团队刚接触与主流语言差异很大的 lisp 时，但这就是软件开发的本质——你在经验中学习。我看的时候确实会畏缩
comments.text: I understand your worry, but I've had a quite opposite take on this. I think we can agree that it's not that hard to find ANY job as an experienced developer. However it's much more difficult to find a great, satisfying job. For that you need to navigate around a lot of corpo-bullshit type of projects, and Clojure has served me well as a useful filter in doing that. My reasoning is that Clojure is niche enough that when company is using it, you can assume that it's due to a deliberate technical choice, and not just because of its popularity. That tells me two things that are symptomatic, in my opinion, of a healthy tech company culture: - tech decisions are made by engineers, not by top-level executives, - their conclusions and bets align with mine because we all see and agree on Clojure's edge over more popular solutions. Admittedly, there's always a risk that someone just followed the hype and got out of their depth but I think this risk is relatively small, because Clojure's no longer a new kid on a block and choosing a tech stack is a major decision and usually done by senior tech leadership, hopefully less hype driven. Of course, Clojure is no silver bullet and it's just a tool that gives you enough rope to hang yourself. Messy codebases are just as possible as in other languages, especially when the team is new to lisps that are very different from mainstream languages, but that's a nature of software development - you learn with the experience.
